d: Piazzetta with several houses and shops still closed. I saw just the dawn, and little by little it goes lightening. Rosina opens the window and shows itself; then Angiolina does the same in his house opposite that of the Rosina; then Giannino comes on the street, playing the guitar and singing.
Angiolina at the window, Giannino on the road.
Bernardo opens the door of his home a little bit, and shows himself to the people, and not to Giannino.
Angioline of the house, with a girl with boxes of the headphones; then Bernardo.
Rosina walks out of the house with her Scolara who brings the work.
Room in Madama's house. Madame Costanza with a mirror in her hand, and then Fabrizio.

Piazzetta as in the previous scenes, with the open workshops of the Fabbro and the Calzolaio, and more in the middle of the open workshop of the Legnaiuolo with the counter outside, and various tables and instruments of such art. Outside the workshop of the Fabbro a petiole anvil, and outside that of the Calzolaio a stone, on which such artists lean to beat the leather; from here and beyond the houses as before. Bernardo at the petiole banquet outside to sit, working in his shoes. Titta by the anvil thinning an iron first with the file, then with the hammer. Giannino at his counter, preparing tables for his works, marking and beating to measure his need; then Angiolina with his Scolara; then Rosina with his.
Room of Bernardo's house with coffee table for Rosina's use, with various works of his craft and straw chairs. Rosina with three School.
Rosina and the three schools, as above.
Madame Costanza's room, Madame Costanza, then a Servant.
Courtyard that introduces to a tavern with table and bench for the use of drinkers. Rosina lonely.
Cheerful wine titta, red Bernardo in the face and mesto and stunned Giannino.
Angiolina and the above, then Rosina.
Madame Costanza's room, Madame Costanza and two servants.
Bernardo and a Servant, then Angiolina.
Garden in Madame Costanza's house. Rosina and Giannino.
Titta, then Madame Costanza and Fabrizio, then Bernardo and Angiolina, then Rosina and Giannino.
